methodology.deduplication: One canonical record per distinct layoff event; corroborating source URLs are retained in the event record.
methodology.headcount: Only numeric figures with a source are included in aggregate headcounts. Undisclosed counts are excluded.
methodology.dates: event_date records when the workforce action was announced or took effect, as explicitly described by sources; publication dates belong to individual source records.
methodology.initial_population_note: Initial population includes Enphase Energy and Skyscanner records verified in the immediately preceding research cycle but not yet published, plus the Oracle European Works Council proposal discovered during catch-up research. The Oracle figure is an unverified reported maximum, not confirmed completed layoffs.
methodology.ai_attribution: Following the Layoffs.fyi AI tracker scope, include events attributed to AI by the company or credible press: to fund AI investment, replace human work with AI, or respond to AI-driven market disruption. Preserve attribution status; press attribution is not company confirmation.
methodology.benchmark_attribution: Layoffs.fyi is linked as an external benchmark with attribution. Fired records remain independently normalized and source-linked; benchmark totals are not merged into Fired aggregates.

events.headline: Oracle reportedly proposes up to 1,390 additional job cuts across the European Economic Area
events.event_date_note: Date of the European Works Council memo; not the date of completed layoffs.
events.geography_note: Country-by-country allocation not disclosed; national consultation processes remain pending.
events.figure_note: The Next Web reported an internal European Works Council memo proposing up to 1,390 cuts. TNW said it could not independently verify the memo; Oracle had been approached for comment. No individual redundancies were final and country-level consultations remain pending.

sources.headline: Oracle plans third round of European job cuts in a year, leaked memo says
Oracle envisage jusqu’à 1 390 suppressions de postes supplémentaires en Europe

events.headline: SAP reportedly weighs at least 10,000 potential job cuts in an AI-era restructuring
events.event_date_note: First public reporting date of the proposal; implementation date and final decision date have not been disclosed.
events.geography_note: Global workforce; country-level allocation has not been disclosed. SAP is headquartered in Walldorf, Germany. Its German labour council negotiated an employment guarantee through 2028.
events.figure_note: Bloomberg reports that SAP is preparing a plan involving at least 10,000 positions, equivalent to at least 9% of its global workforce. The number is not final and may change after labour negotiations. SAP declined to comment on whether job cuts are planned; Reuters said it could not independently verify Bloomberg's report. The 10,000 figure is a reported minimum under consideration, not confirmed completed layoffs.
events.company_response_note: SAP said it continuously reviews its organisation to remain aligned with strategy and customer needs, and declined to comment on whether any job cuts are planned.
